Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Dingo and his friends have gotten lost on Walkabout! Visit their dreams to lead them home! Each turn consists of two steps performed in order: Walkabout (automatic) Dreamtime (player action) Contents 1 Walkabout (Automatic) 2 Dreamtime (Player Action) 3 Goal 4 Game Variants 4.1 Hazards 4.2 Easy 4.3 Dream Companions 4.4 Deep Sleep Walkabout (Automatic) A walkabout card is revealed at random from the deck. The tile in the grid (or the extra tile) with the corresponding landscape (border + picture combination) is automatically flipped over, and your animal is revealed in the location. Dreamtime (Player Action) You click/tap on one of the positions at the edge of the dreamscape grid. This causes the extra tile to slide into the corresponding row or column, thereby shifting the entire row or column of tiles. A new, different tile emerges from the opposite side, to be used for your next action. Goal Be the first player to have your animal revealed in all the locations in the grid matching the marks (spirals) in the Dream Card. This earns you one Victory Point. Play is repeated with a reset grid and a new Dream Card every time, until one player achieves the set number of Victory Points (1, 2, 3 or 4), and claims the final victory. (Also refer to the Deep Sleep variant below) Game Variants Hazards If hazards are turned on, there's an extra goal in addition to the usual goal, for you to earn a victory card: Your animal should NOT be present in the hazard locations - those corresponding to the brown markers in the Dream Card. Easy In this difficulty setting, suitable for beginners or very young children, you only need to make your animal appear in five locations in a line - either in a row, in a column or along a diagonal. Dream Companions If Dream Companions are turned on, there's an extra companion animal tile provided to each player. This adds an additional challenge to the usual goal: Your companion animal should be present in the central location on the grid before you can earn a victory card. Deep Sleep In this variant, play three times . At the end of each play, each player is scored as follows: +1 point per match: Animal on a marked location as in the Dream Card -1 point per match: Animal on a hazard location as in the Dream Card +1 point : Companion positioned in the central location +3 points : Being the first to achieve the goal (considering marks, hazards & companion) At the end of the third play, the player with the highest total score claims victory! [Rating: 2/10] Dingo's Dreams is a game in the tradition of Take It Easy which means it really isn't much of a game at all. Part bingo, part sliding puzzle, there is no interaction whatsoever as each player tries to arrange his or her personal tableau in the requested pattern. Lucky flips will sometimes just drop into place while most of the time you will simply make the most obvious move towards the solution.  The so-called advanced rules are even worse than the standard game for two reasons. Unlucky flips will heavily punish random players and they can actually make the puzzle entirely unsolveable.

[Rating: 2/10] Pretty typical contemporary fare with no player interaction: try to solve a puzzle on your player board whilst a deck of cards throws random pieces at you, potentially helping or sabotage your plans. As you struggle towards completion, one of your opponents will announce they've managed to make the pattern before you - something you had no chance of keeping track of, much less affect in any way.

[Rating: 2/10] An excessively simple and solitaire tile-sliding puzzle. Each player getting their own random grid layout means there's no point in playing it competitively.

[Rating: 2/10] Bingo where you slide the columns and rows to try to form a pattern.  Zero player interaction puzzle with randomness.  More of a game than bingo I guess, but not much. Only played on BGA - with a physical copy, it seems sliding the tiles would be a total pita.

[Rating: 2/10] Feels more like a solitaire puzzle game. Limited player interaction for what it is.

[Rating: 3/10] The game has absolutely zero interaction.  There is not event pacing pressure based on how close someone else is to winning -- knowing someone else's position has NO impact what-so-ever on your own behavior.  NONE.  People claim dominion has no interaction, but there is timing pressure there.  Here, there is truly no interaction.  The game is mechanical and a bit random.  Sometimes the tile you need randomly flips into place.  Most of the time, you make the obvious push to get close to the goal pattern.
